correctness.rationale: Unrestricted affine tetrahedron optimization reduces exactly to four original polytope vertices, because absolute oriented volume is separately convex in each argument. The independently executable integer-polynomial program exhaustively enumerates all 495 unordered quadruples, proves the ten symbolic absolute-determinant forms and counts, and an explicit witness realizes the unique largest form. Positive polynomial gaps prove the strict interior maximum; removed homothetic corner volumes give 1-4t^3. Differentiation gives a quartic numerator strictly increasing on [0,1/2], proving a single sharp global minimum. Rational tests verify boundary and special values; finite checks are not substituted for the universal reduction.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison of Jiao–Torquato (regular truncated-tetrahedron packing) and Di Summa et al. Beck discusses expected random simplex volume and is not a directly covering claimed maximum; full text was not obtained. Mathematical equivalences and stronger generic results were assessed rather than relying on title differences. Historical priority remains uncertain.

value.rationale: Best-contained-simplex fraction is a canonical affine-invariant measure of how faithfully a body is approximated by a tetrahedron. Equal-depth vertex truncation is the natural path linking a tetrahedron, its regular truncated Archimedean solid, and an octahedron. The complete sharp parametric law and its previously non-obvious interior strict minimum quantify an actual geometric phase of worst tetrahedral occupancy, rather than a numerically isolated table entry. The 495-case exact certificate and explicit sharp constructions make the invariant reusable.
